title: Vilasa 2. The Birth and Childhood of Narottama; His Departure for Vrindavana
html:
Narottama's birth in Kheturi; his first feeding and naming; studies and detachment; the brahmana Krishnadasa's accounts of the Lord and of Srinivasa; in a dream the Lord bids Narottama go to Vrindavana; his flight from home

1Glory to Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita with their associates!
Be merciful, Prabhu, to this wretched beggar.

2Glory, glory to the listeners, oceans of mercy!
Hear what I shall now relate.

3Here, after some time, by Prabhu's will,
Narottama was born to manifest bhakti.

4On the full-moon day of the month of Magha, at the sixth danda,1
every auspicious sign came together at the moment of his appearance.

5The mother's beauty increased most wonderfully;
seeing her son, she shed tears of joy.

6The lying-in chamber shone divinely,
and all who were there could not keep still for joy.

7In the village of Sri Kheturi the highest good came about:
evil-mindedness vanished, people were overwhelmed with joy.

8No sound but "Hari! Hari!" was on their lips,
their bodies thrilled, tears streamed from their eyes.

9Bhakti-devi entered the hearts of all,
and all came running, jostling, to Krishnananda's house.

10Everyone brought various gifts,
and the most discerning Datta received all with honour.

11Looking at his son's face, he could not turn his eyes away —
what wondrous happiness was in Krishnananda's heart!

12Sri Krishnananda's father, a most generous man,
gave away much wealth for his grandson's welfare.

13How he satisfied the singers, musicians,
bards, panegyrists and heralds — who could describe?

14What marvels occurred at the moment of his appearance
I cannot describe here for fear of length.

15Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita with their associates
danced — Narayani saw it before her eyes.

16No woman is as fortunate as Narayani,
from whose womb Thakura Narottama was born.

17Day by day Narottama grew like the moon;
seeing her son's face, the mother was always beside herself.

18Fortunate Krishnananda, having gained a jewel of a son,
fed the brahmanas with care every day.

19Looking at his son's face soothed his eyes and heart;
on an auspicious day he performed the rite of first feeding.

20The festivity there was at the first feeding —
is it possible to tell it with one mouth?

21A most fortunate astrologer was there;
on seeing the child his knowledge became clear.

22At the raja's bidding he examined all the auspicious marks
and said, "The name worthy of him is Narottama."

23Hearing this, the brahmanas said, "So it is, so it is:
he is surely the best among men."2

24What the other men and women said at the naming
I cannot relate in detail.

25What happened at the first feeding
I shall tell, and people will be amazed.

26They carefully put rice to the child's mouth,
but he would not eat, turning his face away.

27They tried in many ways, but he would not take it,
and all became greatly worried.

28The astrologer said: "Do not worry about this:
he will never eat anything but food offered to Vishnu."

29At once they brought rice that was Vishnu's prasada,
put it to the son's mouth, and he ate it with delight.

30From that day the raja told everyone:
"Give him nothing but Krishna's prasada."

31From that very day Krishnananda Datta
himself held rice-prasada of Vishnu to be supreme.

32From of old they had the service of a Deity of Sri Krishna;
now his eagerness for that service grew greatly.

33Thus the first feeding took place;
whoever hears of it has his desires fulfilled.

34Some days later the rite of first tonsure was performed,
and they had him taught grammar and other subjects.

35Whoever taught Narottama any branch of learning
had his own doubts dispelled by Narottama's grace.

36Seeing Sri Narottama's conduct, the learned
spoke quietly to one another of his virtues.

37Some said: "He has descended as a portion of a god —
otherwise could a human being have such power?

38At such a tender age he is well trained in every task
and pleases everyone in every way."

39Some said: "Looking at him for just a moment
we forget all our sorrows, and our eyes are soothed."

40Others said: "The prince is so delicate!
We have never seen another so beautiful in every limb."

41Saying many such things, they praised Krishnananda,
and Krishnananda was immersed in the joy of raising his son.

42Seeing that his son was fit in every way,
he always pondered with great joy at heart:

43"I will have my son married and give him the kingdom,
and, like my father, I shall be free of cares."

44Having resolved this, he told the wise kayasthas
to search for a bride for the marriage.

45Meanwhile Narottama, absorbed in prema, in secret
worshipped Krishna, tears flowing from his eyes.

46A deep mood of detachment was ever in his heart;
he could not bear talk of royal pleasures and the like.

47Seeing his son's detachment at every moment,
Krishnananda Raya was greatly worried.

48Nothing but Narottama pleased him;
so too the mother Narayani — her life was in her son.

49They kept guards by their son at all times,
and still fear dwelt constantly in their hearts.

50Narottama, like a prisoner, thought within himself:
"I see no way — how am I to leave home?"

51Thinking thus, he did not reveal his mind;
"What will happen? Gauranga!" he would cry and sigh.

52Crying "Nitai! Advaita!" he would run in all directions,
rolling on the ground, his body grey with dust.

53Raising his arms he called again and again:
"Prabhu, with Your associates deliver me!"

54Thus every day, finding a very secluded place,
he would weep aloud in great distress.

55The deeds of Gaurachandra had spread throughout the world;
he could not get to hear of them, yet he listened attentively.3

56In the village of Sri Kheturi there was an old brahmana
named Krishnadasa, devoted to Krishna.

57He had fully conquered his senses; everyone stood in awe of him,
and no one dared disobey him.

58He too could not do without Narottama;
having finished his service to Krishna, he would secretly go to see him.

59Narottama, with great respect,
falling to the ground in obeisance, would seat him.

60He would ask about Prabhu and His devotees,
and the brahmana told of each one separately.

61The nectar of Chaitanya's early, middle and final pastimes
he narrated to him in order, attentively, in part.4

62The pastimes of Nityananda and Advaitachandra
he told in prema — hearing them, wood and stone melt.

63Pandita Sri Gadadhara, Pandita Srivasa,
Vakreshvara, Svarupa, Murari, Haridasa,

64Narahari Dasa, Gauridasa, Gadadhara,
Vasu Ghosha, Mukunda, Sanjaya, Damodara,

65Kashishvara, Sri Paramananda Bhattacharya,
Krishnadasa Brahmachari, the excellent Lokanatha,

66Sanatana, Rupa, Sri Gopala, Raghunatha,
Raghunatha Bhatta, Jiva, renowned in the world,

67Subuddhi Mishra, Raghava, Krishna Pandita and others —
the accounts of all of them he told as was fitting.

68In the course of it he spoke of Srinivasa Acharya —
how he was born and where.

69As he spoke, tears streamed from both his eyes;
taking Narottama by the hand, the brahmana said:

70"O Narottama, his life is wonderful:
in a short time he became learned in all the shastras.

71An embodiment of prema-bhakti, in great eagerness
he set out for Nilachala to see Sri Chaitanya.

72Some way along he heard of Sri Prabhu's disappearance;
he fell senseless, and only by His will did he remain alive."

73Thus in the Guna-lesha-suchaka of Sri Karnapura Kaviraja:5
He appeared in the house of a foremost brahmana of the Ghanteshvara line of the Rarhi brahmanas;
with a pure intellect expert in many shastras he conquered his opponents while still a boy;
hearing that the feet of Shachi's son were manifest at Niladri, he gave up everything —
may he, Sri Srinivasa Prabhu, my ocean of mercy, be victorious!

74Going to Sri Purushottama, he heard on the way of Chaitanya's disappearance;
falling senseless, tearing his hair, striking his head and reproaching himself,
he placed His feet in his heart and went on to Nilachala by himself —
may he, Sri Srinivasa Prabhu, my ocean of mercy, be victorious!

75"Prabhu consoled him in a dream and brought him to Nilachala;
seeing Srinivasa, all were awash in tears of prema.

76Gadadhara, Vakreshvara, the Pandita and all the others
showed Srinivasa mercy, each as was fitting,

77and all bade him go to Vrindavana.
Having seen Jagannatha, he set out for Gauda.

78Having come to Shrikhanda and setting out again for Nilachala,
on the way he heard of the disappearance of Pandita Gosani.6

79Half dead, he came back to the land of Gauda;
in a dream Sri Pandita consoled him endlessly.

80In the morning, distraught, he went along the road to Gauda,
and there he met people from Gauda.

81Hearing from them of the disappearance of Prabhu Nityananda and Advaita,
he fell unconscious.

82Coming to his senses, he kindled a fire to burn himself,
but the two Prabhus consoled him in a dream

83and bade him go to Vrindavana by way of Gauda;
when the night ended he set out for Gauda.

84Going to Khanda, he bowed to Narahari and Sri Raghunandana,
received their permission and set out at once."

85Thus in the same Guna-lesha-suchaka:
Going on his way, he came to the town called Khanda, bowed to the beloved of Chaitanya-chandra,
the best of Thakuras, Sri Sarakara, and received his permission;
then, bowing at the feet of Raghunandana, he went on, remembering him —
may he, Sri Srinivasa Prabhu, my ocean of mercy, be victorious!

86"Coming to Navadvipa, he saw a marvel:
the manifest pastimes of Gauranga with His associates.

87Astonished, he looked again — and saw
an ocean of sorrow surging in Navadvipa.

88Eagerly Srinivasa went to Prabhu's house,
and there Vishnupriya Devi showed him great mercy.

89Dasa Gadadhara, Srivasa and others
favoured Srinivasa, and all were awash in tears of prema.

90Then, going to Shantipura, he saw Mother Sita —
her motherly affection cannot be described.

91From there, absorbed in prema, he went to Khardaha,
and there Sri Jahnava showed him great mercy.

92He went to Khanakul, to Sri Abhirama,
who together with Malini showed Srinivasa mercy.

93He came again to Shrikhanda, and Sri Narahari
with great affection sent him off to Vraja.

94Sri Raghunandana, overwhelmed with tenderness,
told him all about the way.

95Srinivasa, having consoled his mother at Yajigrama,
a few days ago went alone to Vraja."

96When Narottama heard this account of Srinivasa Acharya,
prema spontaneously arose in his heart.

97Eagerly Narottama thought within himself:
"Who knows after how many days I shall gain his company?"

98As he pondered thus, like the current of a river
the sweetest streams of prema flowed from his eyes.

99Who can understand this way of Narottama's?
Again and again he listened to the lives of Prabhu's devotees.

100He constantly reproached himself
for not having seen such an incarnation of Prabhu.

101He found no peace, his heart was always overflowing;
food did not please him, he passed the nights awake.

102One day, when by Prabhu's will he fell asleep,
Gaura Raya appeared to him face to face in a dream:

103a form enchanting the worlds, an ocean of rasa —
lightning, kunkuma, gold: what can be compared to Him?

104The knot of His curling hair rolled down His back;
even chaste wives lost their modesty on seeing Him.7

105Earrings in His ears, His cheeks gleaming,
tilaka on His forehead — who could keep his life?

106Brows like bows, lotus eyes, the snares of Kama,
a face steeped in smiles that surpasses the full moon.

107Arms reaching to the knees, a broad chest,
lovely necklaces of many gems on a conch-like neck.

108A deep and shapely navel set in three folds,
a slender waist surpassing a lion's.

109Thighs like inverted plantain stems, enchanting even sages,
lovely soles surpassing the lotus.

110He wore an incomparable cloth tucked in three places.
Seeing such wondrous beauty, Narottama

111could not blink; tears streamed from his eyes
like strings of pearls on a lotus.

112His most tender body was filled with thrills,
their lustre surpassing the beauty of kadamba filaments.

113In rapture he fell to the ground and clasped Prabhu's feet,
and Prabhu placed His foot on Narottama's head.

114Spreading out both arms, He embraced him
and, full of affection, spoke sweet words:

115"O Narottama, see, here I am before you!
My heart cannot bear your weeping.

116Do not worry: you will soon go to Vrindavana
and become the disciple of My dear Lokanatha.

117With great joy he will give you the mantra of initiation,
and through you much will be accomplished."

118As He was saying much in this way, the sleep was broken;
without the sight of Prabhu, waves of sorrow surged.

119Distraught, he fell to the ground and rolled about —
and by Prabhu's will sleep drew him in again.

120In the dream he saw: in Navadvipa, on the bank of the Ganga,
Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita joyfully sporting.

121Gadadhara, Srivasa, Svarupa, Narahari,
Haridasa, Vakreshvara, Mukunda, Murari,

122Govinda, Madhava, Vasu Ghosha, Shuklambara,
Gauridasa, Shriman, Sanjaya, Damodara,

123Mahesha, Shankara, Yadu, Acharya-nandana —
the host of devotees surrounded Prabhu and performed sankirtana.

124The people of Navadvipa came running from all sides —
who would not long to see such beauty?

125Brahma, Shiva and Shesha, immeasurably intoxicated with joy,
gazed on that form with unblinking eyes.

126Purandara, with all the gods in heaven,
showered flowers incessantly to see that beauty.

127Gandharvas and kinnaras, mingling with men,
sang of the virtues of Prabhu and His associates, danced and ran about.

128That ocean of prema surged and flooded the worlds —
neither the fallen, nor the low, nor the insentient escaped it.

129Hundreds of thousands of beasts and birds forgot themselves at the sight of that beauty; those blind from birth gained sight and came running.

130Narottama saw this wondrous scene,
and his eyes poured like the current of a river.

131Prabhu Gaurachandra, beholding Narottama,
took him on His lap — and could not restrain His heart.

132He drenched Narottama with the tears of His eyes,
and Narottama fell at Prabhu's feet.

133Lifting him from the ground, Gaurahari, full of affection,
took his hand and entrusted him to Nityananda and Advaita.

134Having had His dear devotees bestow their mercy on him,
He urgently bade him go to Vrindavana.

135Again He said, "Be merciful to him, My dear ones,"
and saying this, sent him off to Vrindavana.

136Narottama could not be still even for an instant
once he glanced at the beauty of Prabhu Nityananda.

137Falling to the ground, he bowed at Prabhu's feet,
and Prabhu placed his holy feet on his head.

138Spreading out his arms, he embraced him
and gave him the priceless treasure of Gauranga's prema.

139He gave him permission to go to Vrindavana
and, seeing him distraught, consoled him greatly.

140Seeing the great beauty of Prabhu Advaita,
Narottama fell at his feet, rolling on the ground.

141Prabhu Sri Advaita could not restrain himself;
lifting him by the hand, he embraced him again and again.

142Entrusting him to the lotus feet of Gauranga,
he commanded, "Go to Vrindavana."

143Gadadhara, Srivasa and the others dear to Prabhu —
seeing their beauty, his eyes blossomed.

144Falling to the ground he bowed at the feet of all,
and all, in prema, embraced Narottama.

145Narottama bathed in the tears from everyone's eyes
and offered his mind and life at the feet of all.

146Prabhu's associates consoled Narottama,
entrusted him to Prabhu's feet and sent him off.

147Just as Narottama was setting out for Vrindavana,
the sleep broke, and his heart was filled with great sorrow.

148Waking, he saw that the night was turning to dawn;
he performed his morning duties and consoled his heart.

149At that time various auspicious omens appeared,
and Narottama in his joy was bathed in tears.

150Meanwhile Narottama's father suddenly
went to Gauda on royal business with many people.

151Narottama knew that this was the auspicious moment,
and on some pretext took leave of his mother.8

152Most prudent, he considered everything carefully
and, eluding the guards, set out in secret.

153Not visiting Navadvipa and other places,
for fear of people he went to Vrindavana by forest paths.

154The Mahashaya disguised himself
so that no one would recognize him if he met anyone.

155Having passed a fifteen days' journey,
his anxiety eased somewhat, and he went on calmly.

156How the mother and father fared here without Narottama —
who could describe it with one mouth?

157Everywhere in Gauda people said to one another:
"The prince Narottama has gone to Vraja.

158The one whom Prabhu drew to Himself in the village of Ramakeli —
this is that Narottama, we now know for certain.

159Otherwise could another have such power,
that whoever saw him lost the fear of worldly existence?"

160People said many such things and wept;
everyone spoke eagerly of Narottama.

161All those dear to Nityananda, Advaita and Chaitanya
prayed constantly for Narottama's welfare.

162Narottama went on unhindered along the highway;
what his displays of prema were like — who could tell?

163He sang the Lord's virtues incessantly,
his eyes pouring like the current of a river.

164Whoever glanced but once at Narottama
was freed from the miseries of worldly life.

165In whatever village Narottama spent the night,
gladness grew in the hearts of the villagers.

166Men and women stayed near Narottama
and spoke softly to one another of many things.

167Some said: "Gold and champaka — let them keep their distance!
Look what a wondrous form is shining!"

168Some said: "What a face, what long eyes,
what a nose, cheeks, brows, forehead, ears!"

169Some said: "What arms, what a broad chest,
a navel in three folds, what a slender waist!"

170Some said: "What knees, what beauty in the feet!
Of what and by whom was he fashioned — with what care!"

171Some said: "This is no ordinary man —
either a god or a king's son."

172Some said: "Alas, at such a tender age,
in such renunciation he wanders from land to land!"

173Some said: "What more can one say —
how will his mother and father keep alive without him?"

174Some said: "Perish the Creator, heartless as he is,
who drove such a boy out of his home!"

175Saying many such things to one another,
they could not leave Narottama and go home.

176They brought various foods and fed him a little with care,
and brought him a fine bed to sleep on.

177But neither food nor sleep pleased Narottama;
in sankirtana of the name he stayed awake all night.

178His body grey with dust, tears in his eyes —
seeing that state, everyone's heart wept.

179At dawn he set out, taking leave of all,
and people ran after him in distress.

180Whoever saw this state of his on the road —
Narottama stole the hearts of all.

181Having seen all the holy places in a short time,
Narottama entered Vrindavana with gladness of heart.

182First he went to Sri Mathura, to the Vishrama-ghata,
bathed in the Sri Yamuna and stayed there.

183A watch of the night had passed and all was deserted,
and in prema he performed sankirtana of the holy name.

184At that time a brahmana of Mathura,
a great Vaishnava, most pure in conduct,

185having offered wonderful foods to Krishna,
fed Narottama, overcome with affection.

186Whatever the brahmana, overwhelmed by fatherly love, asked,
Narottama, won by affection, told him.

187Narottama asked for news of Vraja,
and the brahmana with an aching heart told him everything.

188Hearing that Raghunatha, Kashishvara, Rupa and Sanatana
had disappeared, he wept.

189Uttering the names of Sri Rupa and Sanatana,
he rolled on the ground, his body grey with dust.

190"Kashishvara Pandita! Sri Bhatta Raghunatha!" —
uttering these names, he beat his head with his hands.

191"Alas, alas! What has happened!" he cried again and again,
"I have not seen the holy feet of any of them!"

192Saying many such things, Narottama fainted;
streams flowed from both his eyes like rivers.

193Seeing that he had become as if dead, the best of brahmanas
took Narottama on his lap and wept bitterly.

194After a while the very old and most steady brahmana
composed himself and calmed Narottama.

195In much conversation the night had almost passed,
and by Prabhu's will sleep came over them both.

196In a dream Rupa and Sanatana appeared,
with Raghunatha Bhatta and Kashishvara — all four.

197Narottama, seeing their beauty, awash in tears,
fell at the feet of all, rolling on the ground.

198Then they embraced Narottama with great affection
and drenched Narottama's body with tears of prema.

199They spoke nectarean words of consolation,
and the fortunate brahmana heard some of them.

200All of them, greatly pleased with Narottama,
showed him their mercy and vanished.

201In that separation Narottama's heart lost all composure;
waking, he lamented and looked in every direction.

202"Where have you gone?" he cried, tears streaming from his eyes;
seeing Narottama's state, the brahmana was astonished.

203Eagerly the brahmana took Narottama on his lap
and, crying "I am purified!", was bathed in tears.

204Speaking many sweet words to Narottama,
after a while the old brahmana grew calm.

205Seeing that the night had turned to morning, the best of brahmanas
wanted to take Narottama to his own house.

206Narottama, bowing to the brahmana,
anxiously begged leave again and again:

207"Be merciful to me — I shall go
and see the feet of all the Gosvamis.

208Grant that my longing be fulfilled."
The brahmana affectionately embraced him and blessed him.

209He went some distance with Narottama,
but his feet would not go on — he was very tired.

210Showing Narottama the way to Vrindavana,
he, full of affection, gave him a man as companion.

211Narottama went on, having bowed at the brahmana's feet,
and the brahmana, pained by separation, gazed after him along the road.

212As he walked, Narottama thought to himself:
"They have brought one as unworthy as I to Vrindavana!

213The merciful Prabhu, Sri Gosvami Lokanatha —
will he accept one as fallen as I?

214Sri Gopala Bhatta, Sri Bhugarbha Mahashaya,
Sri Jiva Gosvami and the others, abodes of prema —

215shall I be able to place their lotus feet on my head?
Will they all be merciful to a helpless one like me?

216Srinivasa Acharya, the embodiment of prema —
will he show love to a wretch like me?"

217As soon as he said this, tears of prema flowed from his eyes;
he could not walk, his body tottered.

218Meanwhile, the previous night, Srinivasa suddenly
lost his composure — his heart was pervaded by gladness.

219Seeing great auspicious omens, he thought within himself:
"Surely I shall meet some friend of my life."

220As prema rose of itself his eyes poured,
and for much of the night he joyfully sang the holy name.

221Toward the end of the night he suddenly slept a little,
and in a dream Sri Rupa said to Srinivasa:

222"O Srinivasa! When this night turns to morning,
you will meet Narottama."

223Having said this, the Gosvami vanished;
Srinivasa awoke and saw that the night was over.

224Going quickly to Sri Jiva Gosvami,
he bowed and told him what had happened in the night.

225Sri Jiva Gosani said to Srinivasa:
"In the same way Prabhu has made known to me that he is coming.9

226The one I told you about before —
that very Narottama is coming here.

227I was eager to tell you my dream,
and hearing it from your lips I have gained great happiness."

228Saying this, he hurried to have darshan of Govinda,
and Srinivasa in great joy returned to his own place.

229Suddenly someone came with the news:
"A king's son has come from Gauda.

230He is young, his form is most lovely,
his body is always drenched with tears from his eyes.

231The transformation that came over him at the sight of Sri Govinda —
who can describe it? It is astonishing.

232Sri Jiva Gosvami took him on his lap
and sprinkled his body with the tears of his own eyes.

233Having consoled him with the sweetest words,
he has sent me to fetch you."

234Hearing this, Srinivasa could not keep still,
and with gladness of heart he went to Govinda's gate.

235There he met Narottama —
as a pauper finds a priceless jewel.

236What Srinivasa said as he embraced him
is so sweet that I cannot expand on it here.

237What Narottama became at the sight of the Acharya —
who could describe it with one mouth?

238People said to one another in amazement:
"We have seen a wonder — this natural love."

239Seeing Srinivasa and Narottama together,
they discussed many things among themselves.

240Whatever desire was in Narottama's heart,
Govindadeva fulfilled it.

241Sri Krishna Pandita, the servant of Govinda,
carefully gave him a garland-prasada.

242In passing I shall tell of Krishna Pandita:
he is an associate of Chaitanya, greatly learned.

243When Kashishvara Gosvami disappeared,
Sri Krishna Pandita served the feet of Govinda.

244It is known everywhere that Sri Krishna Pandita Gosvami
had great love for Narottama.

245How Narottama, bowing to Sri Krishna Pandita,
showed humility — hearing of it, the heart weeps.

246Sri Jiva Gosvami quickly took Narottama
to the ashrama of Lokanatha Gosvami.

247He was sitting alone in deep seclusion,
his heart burning in separation from Sanatana and Rupa.

248Sri Jiva Gosvami, bowing, very softly
told the Gosvami about Narottama.

249Hearing and seeing Narottama, he was bathed in tears,
and Narottama fell at the Gosvami's feet.

250Remembering what had gone before, he could not contain his tenderness
and placed his holy feet on Narottama's head.10

251Bathing Narottama in nectarean words,
he let him know that initiation would take place in a few days.

252To Sri Jiva Gosvami he said again and again:
"See to it that he gains eligibility for the books of bhakti."

253And to Srinivasa he said with great tenderness:
"Always keep him attentive on the path of bhakti."

254Having said this, he took the names of Rupa and Sanatana
and, in great distress, heaved long sighs.

255Seeing the Gosvami's state, Sri Jiva Gosani
became such as cannot be described.

256Unable to check his ceaseless tears,
he found a moment and took his leave.

257What happened at the darshan of the lotus feet of Sri Radha-vinoda —
who could describe it?

258What Srinivasa said to Narottama there —
those accounts of prema are described at length elsewhere.

259Having calmed Narottama, Sri Jiva Gosani
quickly took him to Bhatta Gosvami.

260He was sitting alone in deep seclusion,
ever distressed without Rupa and Sanatana.

261What his attitude toward Sanatana was —
what can I say? It is known everywhere.

262Thus in a verse:11
Whose heart is flooded with love for Sanatana,
in whom everything is marked by friendship with Sri Rupa,
who grants the desires of those who worship him, whose only life is Radha-ramana —
to him, Gopala Bhatta, I bow.

263Seeing the Gosvami's state, Sri Jiva Gosani
became such as cannot be described.

264Bowing humbly, he said:
"This is that Narottama," and hearing it, he rejoiced.

265Narottama fell at the Gosvami's feet,
and he embraced him and drenched him with the tears of his eyes.

266Asking after his welfare in the sweetest words,
he showed him such tenderness as I cannot describe.

267Sri Jiva Gosvami, bowing to the Gosvami,
went on, taking Srinivasa and Narottama with him.

268The joy that came as they gazed their fill on the beauty of Sri Radha-ramana —
I cannot tell it.

269Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana —
the face, the chest and the holy feet of these three in turn

270are seen when the darshan of all three is joined together —
so Sri Jiva Gosvami explained to Narottama.12

271Thus, speaking of many things in prema,
they entered the temple of Sri Gopinatha.

272Sri Madhu Pandita informed the Gosvami:13
"Narottama has come from Gauda today."

273Narottama fell at the Gosvami's feet,
and he, greatly delighted, took him on his lap.

274Drenching Narottama with the streams from his eyes,
he spoke to him with such tenderness as I cannot tell.

275He gave him darshan of Radha-Gopinatha
and, bringing a garland-prasada, gave it to Narottama.

276What Narottama became on seeing Gopinatha —
who could describe it?

277Sri Jiva Gosvami took the two of them from there
quickly to the dwelling of Bhugarbha Gosvami.

278He, full of prema, a great and profound scholar,
was one body with Lokanatha Gosvami.

279He sat in seclusion meditating on Prabhu's pastimes;
Sri Jiva Gosvami went and met him there.

280He introduced to him the dear Narottama,
and the Gosvami was filled with supreme joy.

281Narottama fell at Sri Bhugarbha's feet,
and he showed great affection, embracing him.

282Taking Narottama on his lap, he could not let him go;
all that he said I cannot relate in detail.

283Sri Jiva Gosvami, bowing to Sri Bhugarbha,
went to his own place with Srinivasa and Narottama.

284He gave them darshan of Sri Radha-Damodara,
and Narottama, in prema, lost his composure.

285The state he fell into at the sight of Rupa Gosvami's samadhi —
who could describe it?

286Narottama fell to the ground and rolled about;
streams flowed from his eyes like the current of a river.

287His body became motionless, his breath stopped;
Srinivasa hurriedly lifted him onto his lap.

288Sri Jiva Gosvami, after a while bringing him round,
took Narottama to his own hut.

289At that time someone told the Gosvami:
"Come quickly to Govinda's temple."

290As soon as he heard, he went quickly with the two
and saw the arati of Govinda's raja-bhoga.

291There they partook of maha-prasada
and again came back to his dwelling, the two with him.14

292After spending a while in talks about Krishna,
they went to have darshan of Sri Madanamohana.

293Going there, they saw the arati of awakening,
and he told everyone about Narottama.

294Krishnadasa Brahmachari Gosvami, with affection,
showed him such mercy as I cannot describe at length.

295Narottama, seeing Sri Madanamohana,
could not hold himself up; streams flowed from his eyes.

296The pujari Gosani gave him a garland-prasada —
what happiness there was cannot be told.

297Where the samadhi of Sanatana Gosvami is,
Sri Jiva himself showed Narottama.

298What Narottama became at the sight of the samadhi —
who could describe it with one mouth?

299Who can describe Sri Jiva Gosvami's tenderness!
He calmed Narottama in many ways.

300With them all Sri Jiva Gosvami went to his dwelling
and entrusted Narottama to his dear Srinivasa.

301In great happiness Srinivasa took Narottama,
bowed to the Gosvami and went to his own place.

302The two passed the night in the relish of talks about Krishna,
and at dawn bathed in the Yamuna, absorbed in prema.

303Having bowed at the feet of their own worshipful Deities,
they joyfully went to Sri Jiva Gosvami.

304He quickly sent them to Radha-kunda,
and they went and saw the sweetness of the two kundas.

305Srinivasa went to Dasa Gosvami
and carefully told him about Narottama.

306Though the Gosvami's heart was in great distress,
still, hearing this, he felt joy arise.

307"Where is Narottama?" he said and opened his eyes,
and Narottama went and bowed at his lotus feet.

308Overwhelmed with tenderness, Sri Dasa Gosani
showed him such mercy as cannot be described.

309With all the very wise ones who were there
Narottama met.

310Sri Raghava Pandita Gosani at Govardhana
attained supreme bliss on seeing Narottama.

311Srinivasa and Narottama, having gone everywhere,
came and reported it all to Sri Jiva Gosvami.

312Sri Jiva Gosvami, hearing it all, was pleased
and quickly had Narottama begin his studies.

313Narottama studied the books of bhakti,
stealing the hearts of all by his skill in explaining their meaning.

314Who can understand Narottama's heart?
He was intent on serving Lokanatha Gosvami.

315How he served cannot be put into words;
the Gosani was pleased with Narottama's service.

316One day, seeing Narottama distraught,
he fulfilled his longing by giving him the mantra of initiation.

317What that wondrous mantra and rite of initiation were
I cannot expand on: the shastras of bhakti are the authority for it.

318In Vrindavana everyone rejoiced
to see Narottama's wonderful eligibility.

319Sri Jiva Gosvami, understanding everyone's wish,
gave him the title "Sri Thakura Mahashaya."

320Hearing the lovely title "Sri Thakura Mahashaya,"
all the great souls rejoiced at heart.

321"As is Narottama, so is his title" —
this saying spread everywhere.

322Who does not weep at the virtues of Sri Thakura Mahashaya?
He was the object of everyone's deep affection in Vraja.

323What his way of service in the mind was in Vrindavana
is all made known in the book Bhakti-ratnakara.15

324For fear of length I cannot describe it here;
now I shall tell how he came back again to Gauda.

325Listen to all this continually and with care:
Narahari tells the Narottama-vilasa.

Thus ends the second vilasa of the Narottama-vilasa.

Notes

  1. A danda is twenty-four minutes; the sixth danda is about two and a half hours after sunrise. Both editions read "মাঘ পূর্ণিমা." Tradition usually gives Magha Purnima as Narottama's appearance day; the Prema-vilasa differs (ev-narottama-birth).
  2. A play on words: nara-uttama, "the best of men."
  3. That is, in the guarded house he had no way of hearing about Gaura, yet he caught every word of it.
  4. "Early, middle and final" follows the 1924 edition; the 2021 edition has "early and middle."
  5. Karnapura Kaviraja was a disciple of Srinivasa Acharya; his praise of Srinivasa is also quoted in the Bhakti-ratnakara. Not to be confused with Kavi Karnapura, the son of Shivananda Sena.
  6. Pandita Gosani is Gadadhara Pandita. Srinivasa's journey is told at length in BR 3–4; cf. Prema-vilasa 4–6.
  7. A hyperbole customary in describing the Lord's (as Krishna's) beauty: none can withstand His form; attraction to Him is not worldly passion but the awakening of prema.
  8. "On some pretext" (প্রকারে) — the text does not specify.
  9. That is, Jiva too had been told in a dream of Narottama's coming.
  10. "What had gone before": the Lord's prophecy in the dream about his future disciple Narottama (Vilasa 1).
  11. Neither edition names the source of the verse.
  12. According to tradition, the form of Krishna manifested by Vajranabha is divided among the three Deities of Vrindavana: the face is Govinda's, the chest Gopinatha's, the feet Madanamohana's.
  13. Madhu Pandita, the servant of the Deity Gopinatha in Vrindavana.
  14. That is, Jiva returned to his dwelling together with Srinivasa and Narottama.
  15. "Service in the mind" (manasi-seva): inner service of Radha and Krishna in meditation; Narottama's service in Vrindavana is told at greater length in the Bhakti-ratnakara.
